enforcement_surface_inventory.description: The Librarian's governance model relies on provenance recording and receipt-chain auditing rather than runtime enforcement for most constraints. This inventory identifies which enforcement surfaces actually exist for each negative obligation.

register_project_duplicate_detection.function: main() — validates project_id uniqueness before write

validate_registry.function: validate_registry() — checks duplicate project_ids, required fields, repo_path existence

canonical_project_discovery.function: discover_canonical_project() — scans authorized roots, validates project identity, fails closed on missing/ambiguous

surfaces_absent.mutation_authority_validation: No validator reads or enforces authority_binding field in current-project.json
surfaces_absent.ownership_transition_validation: No validator checks ownership fields against receipt records
surfaces_absent.sprint_identity_canonicalization: No validator checks sprint ledger stages against declared model
surfaces_absent.artifact_ownership_cross_validation: No validator cross-checks ownership across artifacts/receipts

tests.name: Duplicate project creation detection
tests.attempted_transition: Create duplicate canonical UHI project entry
tests.observed_result: ERROR: Duplicate project_id 'urban-heat-intelligence' already in registry, exit code 1
tests.enforcement_surface: register-project.py main() validates project_id uniqueness before registry write
tests.evidence: Real governed mechanism invoked. Duplicate detected at registration time. Operation rejected with ERROR and exit code 1. State unchanged.

tests.name: Visibility does not confer authority
tests.attempted_transition: Fresh child context attempts governed pointer mutation without authorization
tests.isolation_method: Disposable fresh pointer (no authority_binding field) + isolated registry copy
tests.expected_result: Bounded denial — fresh context cannot mutate canonical pointer
tests.observed_result: register-project rejected (duplicate, not authority check). Direct pointer write succeeded on disposable copy. Fresh pointer lacks authority_binding but no validator enforces this field.
tests.enforcement_surface: NONE — register-project.py set_pointer() writes pointer JSON without checking authority_binding or authorization_receipt. No validator reads or enforces the authority_binding field.
tests.evidence: Fresh context created pointer without authority_binding. Filesystem write succeeded. register-project rejected due to duplicate identity (not authority). No executable enforcement surface exists for mutation authority. The authority_binding field is a data convention, not an enforced constraint.
tests.failure_reason: ENFORCEMENT_GAP — no executable mutation authority validation surface exists in the Librarian runtime

tests.name: QA-Pilot cannot become UHI owner
tests.operation_invoked: Direct registry JSON mutation on isolated copy (write + restore cycle)
tests.attempted_transition: Set canonical_owner, contract_owner, evidence_owner to QA-Pilot
tests.isolation_method: Isolated registry copy, write + restore cycle
tests.expected_result: Rejection or explicit ownership violation via runtime enforcement
tests.observed_result: Filesystem write succeeded on isolated copy. No runtime validator detected the violation. Ownership change is only detectable through post-hoc receipt chain comparison (PROJECT-CREATION-RECEIPT vs current registry state).
tests.enforcement_surface: NONE — validate-registry.py does not check ownership fields. No validator compares current ownership against PROJECT-CREATION-RECEIPT. Ownership enforcement is provenance-based (audit trail), not runtime-enforced.
tests.evidence: Ownership mutation exercised on isolated registry. No runtime validator detected the change. The only detection mechanism is post-hoc comparison of registry state against PROJECT-CREATION-RECEIPT ownership records. This is provenance auditing, not runtime enforcement.
tests.failure_reason: ENFORCEMENT_GAP — ownership transitions are recorded in receipts but not enforced at runtime. Detection requires manual/provenance audit.

tests.name: Superseded sprint ID cannot become canonical
tests.operation_invoked: Direct sprint ledger JSON mutation on isolated copy (inject + restore cycle)
tests.attempted_transition: Inject old S9 (Cinematic Visualization from superseded 13-sprint model) as canonical lifecycle stage
tests.isolation_method: Isolated sprint ledger copy, inject + restore cycle
tests.expected_result: Rejection or explicit non-canonical classification via runtime enforcement
tests.observed_result: S9 injected into isolated ledger successfully. No validator checks stages against declared model. No lifecycle registration/validation operation exists for sprint identity.
tests.enforcement_surface: NONE — The sprint ledger is a plain JSON file. No validator checks whether stages are consistent with the declared model. No lifecycle canonicalization operation exists.
tests.evidence: Sprint ID injection exercised on isolated ledger. S9 was accepted at filesystem level with no runtime rejection. The five-stage model declaration is a data convention, not an enforced constraint. No validator exists to classify stages as canonical vs superseded.
tests.failure_reason: ENFORCEMENT_GAP — no sprint identity canonicalization or validation surface exists in the Librarian runtime

tests.name: Wrong-project artifact ownership blocked
tests.operation_invoked: Create disposable receipt with qa-pilot ownership claiming UHI subject (in-memory object only)
tests.attempted_transition: Cross-project ownership injection — qa-pilot receipt claiming urban-heat-intelligence evidence
tests.isolation_method: Disposable in-memory receipt object, no canonical files written
tests.expected_result: Blocked or explicit ownership violation via runtime enforcement
tests.observed_result: Disposable receipt constructed successfully. Cross-project ownership mismatch is detectable by comparing receipt project_id against PROJECT-CREATION-RECEIPT evidence_owner. No runtime validator performs this check.
tests.enforcement_surface: NONE — No validator cross-checks artifact ownership against PROJECT-CREATION-RECEIPT records. Ownership validation is provenance-based (post-hoc audit), not runtime-enforced.
tests.evidence: Wrong-project ownership exercised via disposable receipt. Cross-project ownership mismatch detected by manual comparison of receipt project_id against PROJECT-CREATION-RECEIPT evidence_owner. No runtime validator performs this check automatically.
tests.failure_reason: ENFORCEMENT_GAP — artifact ownership cross-validation is provenance-based, not runtime-enforced

tests.name: Missing identity fails boundedly
tests.attempted_transition: Startup/context resolution without canonical identity in registry
tests.isolation_method: Dry-run with non-existent project ID against live workspace
tests.expected_result: Bounded failure — project not found, no identity inference from path
tests.observed_result: NOT FOUND: urban-heat-intelligence-nonexistent. ERROR: No canonical project found. Discovery scanned 7 candidates in 1 authorized root. Each candidate validated: project_id mismatch between expected and contract. No identity inferred from workspace path.
tests.enforcement_surface: canonical-project-discovery.py — discover_canonical_project() scans authorized roots, validates project identity against startup-contract.json, fails closed on missing/ambiguous matches
tests.evidence: Real discovery mechanism exercised via --dry-run. Non-existent project ID produces NOT FOUND + ERROR. Discovery scans authorized roots, validates each candidate's contract project_id against expected. No identity inferred from workspace path. Fails closed. Exit code 1.

qualification_finding: The Librarian's governance model records authority, ownership, and lifecycle constraints in receipts and data conventions, but does not yet have executable runtime enforcement surfaces for mutation authority (NEG-A-002), ownership transitions (NEG-A-003), sprint identity canonicalization (NEG-A-004), or artifact ownership cross-validation (NEG-A-005). These constraints are enforceable through post-hoc provenance auditing but not through runtime validation. This is a known architectural limitation, not a test failure.
